stages.label: Curious
intro: You are welcome here before you know where this journey is leading. Curiosity does not need to arrive with a declaration.
Begin with the perspective behind the writing, then spend time with one person’s experience of faith. These are lived reflections, not a course or a case you are expected to accept.

reading.note: Begin with the person speaking, and the boundaries of what these reflections offer.
Stay with uncertainty without requiring the whole road to become visible.
If you wish, read one person’s account of what faith changed inside an ordinary life.

stages.label: Beginning
stages.deck: Approaching Islam, or newly within it.
intro: A beginning can hold questions as well as certainty. You may be approaching shahada, or learning how a decision already made fits into your days.
These reflections stay with belonging, learning and private faith. You bring a whole life with you; there is no expectation that you arrive complete.

reading.note: The emotional weight of feeling watched while learning.
A longer perspective on what changed, and what remained human, in the first year.
A small, personal moment of gratitude.

stages.label: Becoming
stages.deck: Learning how faith lives in ordinary days.
intro: Faith meets the day you actually have: its gratitude, its impatience, its longings, and the moments you wish you had handled differently.
Here, learning is part of living. These pieces leave room for both.

reading.note: On wanting more without denying what has already been given.
A poem about choosing what a moment needs, even when you could have been right.
On comfort, responsibility and becoming more aware of who you are trying to be.

stages.label: Returning
stages.deck: Reconnecting after distance, difficulty or fatigue.
intro: Return can mean coming back to Allah, to a question, to yourself, or to a place where you can think honestly again.
These pieces offer company for tiredness and beginning again. You do not have to turn your return into a performance.

reading.note: A difficult day, with no lesson forced upon it.
Looking for something recognisable when the road feels uncertain.
An honest account of a day that has not been kind.
A reflection on carrying a season’s quiet into the days that follow.

paths.label: I am curious about Islam
paths.deck: You are allowed to explore honestly.
intro: You do not have to call yourself Muslim yet to be welcome here. You can be curious, unsure, or simply trying to understand what keeps drawing your attention.
These are personal accounts of faith being lived. There is no decision to make at the end of a page. Read with your questions still open.

reading.note: Begin with the person speaking, and the boundaries of what these reflections offer.
Stay with uncertainty without requiring the whole road to become visible.
If you wish, read one person’s account of what faith changed inside an ordinary life.

paths.label: I don’t feel Muslim enough
paths.deck: There is a whole life behind your starting point.
intro: A small correction can touch something much larger: the fear that you have not earned your place yet.
These pieces stay with the vulnerability of learning in front of others, and the difference between being seen and being measured.

reading.note: Start with the uncertainty that appeared when something intimate became visible to other people.
Stay with a longer account of belonging, accountability and a faith that did not erase difficulty.
End, if you wish, with a few private words addressed to Allah.

paths.label: I am afraid
intro: Sometimes it is the moment itself. Sometimes it is the fear of who we might become inside it.
Here are reflections on anticipating fear, making a decision without certainty, and leaving space for tiredness when an answer has not arrived.

reading.note: A personal account of leaving before anything has happened, and learning to remain.
A short reflection on making an honest choice before knowing whether it will hold.
There is room here for a difficult day that has not become a lesson yet.

paths.label: I feel alone
paths.deck: Being needed is not always the same as being known.
intro: There can be people around you and still be parts of yourself that have nowhere to go.
These pieces begin with that distance: the care we give, the care we need, and the traces of love we carry with us.

reading.note: On being valued for steadiness while needing someone to offer that same steadiness in return.
A poem about tenderness that asks nothing, and a moment of being allowed to be.
A longer reflection on the ordinary gestures through which a mother’s care remains present.
Meet the voice behind this space: still learning, still questioning, still inside the journey.

paths.label: I need hope
paths.deck: A little light, without a perfect ending.
intro: These pieces do not ask you to explain away a difficult day. They move between an imagined landscape, a changed understanding of gratitude, and one small step.

reading.note: Watch the film or read its words. The landscape gives the feeling of light somewhere to live.
On being thankful for the life you have while still admitting what you long for.
A short thought to carry away, without having to see the whole road.

paths.label: I am finding my way back
paths.deck: You can return with things still unresolved.
intro: Perhaps you have been distant. Perhaps you are simply tired. You do not have to explain all of it before you read.
This selection follows tiredness, the search for direction, and the possibility of beginning again.

reading.note: Begin with the day when meaning could wait, and kindness had to be enough.
A reflection on recognising a direction without knowing the destination.
An unfinished day, anger, and the possibility of meeting tomorrow differently.

paths.label: I just need somewhere quiet
intro: You can stay with one piece. You can leave a page unfinished. These small observations make room for a moment that does not have to become anything else.

reading.note: An ordinary room, a change in the light, and a little attention.
A reflection that gives stillness a landscape of its own.
For when you do not have the energy to turn the day into an explanation.

worlds.label: The Light
intro: Light appears here as a film, a quiet prayer, a change in how gratitude feels. Each piece comes from personal reflection.
You can watch, read, or remain with a few words. There is no order you need to complete.

reading.note: The original film and the words that gave it direction.
A private expression of thanks.
A reflection on gratitude and longing sharing the same prayer.
On looking for a direction before the whole road is visible.

arrivals.label: When the light stays with you
arrivals.deck: From a moment on screen to a little more space.
intro: The film gives hope a landscape: darkness, water, and light that becomes visible as you move toward it.
If that feeling brought you here, begin with the film’s words, then follow the question of direction into a longer reflection.

reading.note: Return to the film and read the words at your own pace.
Stay with the question beneath the image: what can guide us when we cannot see the destination?
Make room, too, for the days when the meaning is not yet clear.

arrivals.label: When gratitude still has room for longing
arrivals.deck: Stay with the thought a little longer.
intro: The sentence on screen begins with a tension: being grateful for what is, while still wanting something more.
Here, the reflection has room to hold both. A longer essay then follows gratitude into the ordinary details of a year.

reading.note: Read the full reflection behind the film, including the prayer it eventually becomes.
Continue into gratitude as a way of noticing a life, rather than a list of things received.

arrivals.label: When being seen feels like being judged
arrivals.deck: There is more behind the photograph.
intro: A correction can land far beyond the detail it was meant to address. The question can become whether the person learning is being seen at all.
These reflections make space for that difference, and for the life that came before faith.

reading.note: Read the reflection behind the carousel, in its full context.
Stay with a broader account of belonging after a year within Islam.
Follow the question of being seen into the relationships we live outside the photograph.

trust.title: Before You Read
trust.deck: You are welcome here before you have everything figured out.

sections.title: A lived perspective.
paragraphs: Moon Confessions comes from lived experience: faith as it meets an ordinary life, with its fear, doubt, gratitude, grief and moments of belonging.
It offers companionship, honest reflection and a personal perspective. It is not a religious authority, and personal experience is not a religious ruling.

sections.title: Room for your questions.
paragraphs: You do not have to call yourself Muslim yet to be welcome here. You can be curious, be uncertain, or be finding your way back.
You do not need to agree with everything you read. There is no expectation that reading here will lead you to a particular decision.

sections.title: When reflection is not enough.
paragraphs: Some questions need more than one person’s story. For religious knowledge, rulings or interpretation, consult qualified sources and people with the relevant learning.
The writing here can sit beside that learning. It cannot take its place.
